item.title: New telescope will help scientists study a mysterious force called 'dark energy'
item.description: NPR's Ayesha Rascoe asks science reporter Joe Palca about the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, which will have a field of view at least 100 times larger than Hubble Space Telescope.

item.title: 'A glorious dawn launch': NASA's newest space telescope has left the Earth
item.description: The tour-bus-sized telescope aims to unravel cosmic mysteries and identify more than 100,000 planets beyond our solar system.

item.title: NASA is about to launch a space telescope that could change how we see the universe
item.description: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launches Aug. 30 on a mission to explore some of the most pressing mysteries of the cosmos.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: NASA's latest telescope will explore dark energy and other cosmic mysteries
item.description: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, set to launch this weekend, may shed new light on the nature of dark energy -- that mysterious force causing the universe to expand.
item.content:encoded: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, set to launch this weekend, may shed new light on the nature of dark energy -- that mysterious force causing the universe to expand.

item.title: A NASA telescope is slowly plummeting to earth and there's no way to save it
item.description: NASA's Swift Observatory has orbited the Earth since 2004. It's now falling towards earth, and after a failed mission to save it, NASA is leaving the doomed telescope to its fate.
item.content:encoded: NASA's Swift Observatory has orbited the Earth since 2004. It's now falling towards earth, and after a failed mission to save it, NASA is leaving the doomed telescope to its fate.

item.title: This high-speed star is whipping around the black hole in the middle of our galaxy
item.description: Researchers have identified a speed demon at the heart of the Milky Way. This fast-moving star may yield insights into the black hole parked at the center of our galaxy.

item.title: Photos: See the best photos from this year's total solar eclipse
item.description: Millions of people in Europe stepped outside Wednesday to watch a spectacular sunset with a solar eclipse. The path of totality passed through portions of Greenland, Iceland, Spain and Portugal.

item.title: Solar eclipse and meteor shower will dazzle onlookers Wednesday
item.description: While parts of Greenland and Western Europe savor a total solar eclipse, much of the Northern Hemisphere will be able to see the peak of the Perseid meteor shower Wednesday night.

item.title: What kind of problem is 34,000 pieces of space junk circling the Earth?
item.description: A derelict SpaceX rocket plowed into the moon Aug. 8, reigniting a debate about space junk. NPR's Ayesha Rascoe talks to John Crassidis from the University at Buffalo about the issue.
